title: Is Organic Food Worse For You?
summary: Explainer arguing organic farms still use pesticides, yield less, offer no meaningful nutrition gain and may carry more bacterial risk, though some practices help soil.

assertions.quote: the truth is, organic farmers can still use pesticides and fungicides
some natural pesticides are actually a more serious health and environmental risk than man-made ones
If a label simply says ‘organic’ it only has to contain 95% organic ingredients.
The label “made with organic ingredients” on items like bread may only contain 70%
the term “free range” also only requires evidence of access to the outdoors for a minimum of 5 minutes per day
organic crop yields are 25% lower on average than conventional ones
organic fruit and veggies are no more nutritious than conventionally grown food
Children placed on organic diets for ten days have lower levels of organophosphates in their urine
both levels are orders of magnitude lower than the amount needed to cause clinical harm
An bag of organic chips, for example, is still just deep fried carbohydrates with very little nutritional value.
Most surprising is that organic food has a higher incidence of being dangerous.

verdicts.note: Systematic review (abstract only): E. coli risk did not differ for produce, and bacterial contamination of retail chicken and pork was common but unrelated to farming method.

assertions.quote: many organic farming practices like crop rotations and mixed planting as opposed to using mono-cultures are better for the soil
